method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Oral/enteral is preferred.** Hypophosphataemia may be asymptomatic — **monitor phosphate in high-risk scenarios.** ⚠️ **Acute severe hypophosphataemia can be life-threatening.** Check other electrolytes and renal function.
claims.source_text: Oral/enteral is the preferred route of phosphate administration Hypophosphataemia may be asymptomatic. Phosphate levels should be monitored in high-risk clinical scenarios Acute severe hypophosphataemia can be a life-threatening medical emergency Assess for other electrolyte abnormalities and renal function
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The lower limit of normal falls with age** — about 1.5 mmol/L in early infancy to 0.8 mmol/L by late adolescence; ranges vary by age and assay.
claims.source_text: The lower limit of normal for serum phosphate changes over childhood, from around 1.5mmol/L in early infancy to 0.8mmol/L by late adolescence Reference ranges vary substantially by age and assay
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severe acute (under 0.5 mmol/L):** weakness, lethargy, paraesthesia. ⚠️ **Below 0.3 mmol/L is a life-threatening emergency.**
claims.source_text: Severe acute hypophosphataemia ( <0.5 mmol/L) may be associated with weakness, lethargy and paraesthesia Serum phosphate below 0.3mmol/L represents a life-threatening medical emergency
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Requirements are higher in childhood, especially in premature infants;** phosphate balance is closely tied to calcium.
claims.source_text: Phosphate requirements depend on bone formation and growth rate. They are higher in childhood, especially in premature infants Phosphate balance is closely related to calcium homeostasis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Redistribution causes to watch for:** refeeding syndrome, DKA, insulin/glucose therapy, sepsis, respiratory alkalosis, hungry bone syndrome. **IV iron infusion** reduces renal reabsorption.
claims.source_text: Internal redistribution between body compartments refeeding syndrome diabetic ketoacidosis insulin/glucose therapy sepsis respiratory alkalosis hungry bone syndrome … Decreased renal phosphate reabsorption IV iron infusion
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess renal function** (urine output, UEC) and **baseline calcium and albumin** — severe hypophosphataemia may cause hypercalcaemia.
claims.source_text: Assess renal function (urine output, serum urea, electrolytes and creatinine). Check baseline serum calcium and albumin levels. Severe hypophosphataemia may cause hypercalcemia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lethargy may be the only symptom.** If the cause is unclear, consider PTH, urine phosphate excretion, and CK (if severe).
claims.source_text: lethargy may be the only symptom present if underlying cause not evident, consider checking parathyroid hormone level, urine phosphate excretion and creatine kinase (for severe hypophosphataemia)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Features:** respiratory muscle dysfunction · arrhythmias · weakness, bone pain, altered mental state, seizure, coma · **haemolytic anaemia** · rickets.
claims.source_text: Respiratory: respiratory muscle dysfunction, decreased oxygen delivery Cardiac: arrhythmias, chest pain Neuromuscular: muscle weakness, bone pain, altered mental status, seizure, arthralgia, coma Haematological: haemolytic anaemia, impaired leukocyte and platelet function Endocrine: rickets eg limb bowing or radiological finding
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat the cause and aim for the normal range.** ⚠️ **Reduce the dose in renal impairment and seek specialist advice;** adjust to response and tolerance.
claims.source_text: Treatment should be directed at the underlying cause with an aim to return serum phosphate levels to the normal range Reduce the dose in children with renal impairment. Seek specialist advice Adjust dose as needed for response and tolerance
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral for mild to moderate asymptomatic hypophosphataemia.** **Neonate: 1 mmol/kg/day in 2–4 divided doses** (up to 3 mmol/kg/day for osteopenia of prematurity). **Child: 2–3 mmol/kg/day in 2–4 divided doses.**
claims.source_text: Consider for mild to moderate asymptomatic hypophosphataemia Dose Neonate: 1mmol/kg/day in 2-4 divided doses higher doses (up to 3mmol/kg/day) are used for osteopenia of prematurity Child: 2-3mmol/kg/day in 2-4 divided doses
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Usual maximum:** under 5 years 3 tablets daily · over 5 years 6 tablets daily · adolescent/adult 1–2 tablets 2–3 times a day.
claims.source_text: Usual maximum dose Age <5 years: 3 tablets daily Age >5 years: 6 tablets daily Adolescent/adult: 1-2 tablets 2-3 times per day
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Phosphate effervescent tablet (500 mg phosphorus) = 16.1 mmol phosphate**, plus sodium 20.4 mmol and potassium 3.1 mmol. **Part doses:** disperse one tablet in 20 mL water (0.8 mmol/mL) and measure immediately.
claims.source_text: Phosphate effervescent tablets (500mg elemental phosphorus) 16.1mmol Also contains: Sodium 469mg (20.4mmol) Potassium 123mg (3.1mmol) … For doses less than a whole tablet: disperse one tablet in 20mL of water to make a concentration of 0.8mmol/mL (25mg/mL) of phosphate. Mix until an even dispersion is formed and measure the required dose immediately
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral adverse effects:** GI upset, over-correction, hypocalcaemia, hypernatraemia, and ⚠️ **acute phosphate nephropathy leading to acute renal failure.**
claims.source_text: abdominal pain, diarrhoea, nausea and vomiting hyperphosphatemia (over-correction), hypocalcaemia, hypernatraemia renal nephrocalcinosis (acute phosphate nephropathy) leading to acute renal failure
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider IV for symptomatic or severe hypophosphataemia**, or when oral is contraindicated (severe malabsorption, nil by mouth). ⚠️ **Seek specialist advice.**
claims.source_text: Intravenous phosphate replacement should be considered for Symptomatic or severe hypophosphataemia Contraindication to oral dosing (eg severe malabsorption or nil by mouth) Precautions Seek specialist advice for intravenous phosphate replacement
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider cardiac monitoring** (potassium content; rapid IV or overdose risks arrhythmia or arrest). **Check phosphate and potassium before and about 2 hours after the infusion.** ⚠️ **Not through the same access or lumen as magnesium- or calcium-containing fluids, including PN.**
claims.source_text: Cardiac monitoring should be considered due to potassium content, rapid intravenous administration or overdose has risk of arrhythmia/cardiac arrest Check serum phosphate and potassium before infusion and approximately 2 hours after completion Do not infuse via same IV access point or lumen as magnesium or calcium-containing intravenous fluids including parenteral nutrition
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Dose: 0.36 mmol/kg by slow infusion.** Doses over 10 mmol need senior approval. **Repeat if required to max 2 mmol/kg/day (max 70 mmol/day).**
claims.source_text: 0.36mmol/kg as slow infusion Doses greater than 10mmol must be approved by a senior clinician The dose may be repeated, if required, up to a maximum of 2mmol/kg/day (maximum 70mmol/day)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mind the potassium:** if K is near the top of normal or above, use a potassium-free formulation where available; **reserve potassium dihydrogen phosphate for children who also need IV potassium.**
claims.source_text: For patients with potassium levels near upper end of normal range or above, use phosphate formulation without potassium where available Reserve potassium dihydrogen for patients requiring intravenous potassium replacement
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IV products:** potassium dihydrogen phosphate **1 mmol/mL phosphate + 1 mmol/mL potassium** · sodium and potassium phosphate **0.67 mmol/mL** (+ potassium 0.13, sodium 1.07 mmol/mL) · sodium dihydrogen phosphate **1 mmol/mL** (+ sodium 1 mmol/mL).
claims.source_text: Potassium Dihydrogen Phosphate (10mL vial) 1mmol/mL Also contains: Potassium 1mmol/mL Sodium Phosphate and Potassium Phosphate Concentrated Injection (20mL vial) 0.67mmol/mL Also contains: Potassium 0.13mmol/mL Sodium 1.07mmol/mL Sodium Dihydrogen Phosphate Injection (10mL vial) 1mmol/mL Also contains: Sodium 1mmol/mL
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Dilute before use: peripheral 0.05 mmol/mL or weaker, central 0.12 mmol/mL or weaker. Infuse slowly over 6 hours; never faster than 0.2 mmol/kg/hour or 10 mmol/hour.** Mix thoroughly to prevent pooling.
claims.source_text: Dilute before use Peripheral line: dilute to 0.05mmol/mL or weaker Central line: dilute to 0.12mmol/mL or weaker Give via slow infusion over 6 hours The rate of administration must not exceed 0.2mmol/kg/hour or 10mmol/hour Careful and thorough mixing after dilution is essential to prevent pooling of phosphate solutions
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IV adverse effects:** over-correction, bradycardia, hypotension, arrhythmia, **hyperkalaemia, hypocalcaemia**, AKI, dyspnoea, oedema, extravasation.
claims.source_text: Monitor for risk of hyperphosphataemia (due to over-correction) Adverse effects may include: Bradycardia, hypotension, arrhythmias Hyperkalaemia, hypocalcemia Acute kidney injury Dyspnoea, oedema Extravasation injury
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Paediatric team** if symptomatic or significantly abnormal; **renal team** if renal dysfunction; **consider transfer** if symptomatic or needing monitoring your centre cannot provide.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when The child is symptomatic or there is a significant abnormality Consider consultation with renal team when Renal dysfunction is present Consider transfer when The child is symptomatic or requires close monitoring not available in your centre
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge** when stable with a management plan and any acute abnormality has resolved.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when The child is clinically stable with an appropriate management plan in place Any acute abnormality has resolved
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hypophosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hypophosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23
